definitions.explanation: The basic verb for dying. Can be used for people, animals, or plants. In polite contexts, 亡くなる (nakunaru) is often preferred when speaking about people.

examples.japanese: その{犬|いぬ}は{去年|きょねん}{死|し}にました。
{花|はな}が{死|し}んでしまった。
{祖父|そふ}は{十年前|じゅうねんまえ}に{死|し}にました。
examples.english: My grandfather died ten years ago.
examples.notes: In more polite speech, 亡くなりました would be used

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). No pair verb. Pattern: Xが{死|し}ぬ (X dies).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {死|し}んでいる = 'is dead' (state, not process of dying).

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{病気|びょうき}で{死|し}ぬ (die of illness)
・{事故|じこ}で{死|し}ぬ (die in an accident)
・{死|し}にそう (about to die - also used hyperbolically)
・{死|し}んでしまった (has died - regret)

One of few godan verbs ending in ぬ. Past: {死|し}んだ (not {死|し}にた). Euphemism: {亡|な}くなる (to pass away) - more polite for people.
